title: Parity sieve (Kuperberg pairing with held-out parity) for every N, time 2^((17/6) sqrt n) n^5 log n

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, the parity sieve PSieve of proof.md (Kuperberg-style low-bit pairing of labeled qubits with exact Hadamard-test Fourier labels, held-out parity and anchored odd-multiplier decoder; parameters d = ceil((3/4) sqrt n), l = ceil((n-3)/d), stage targets T^(j)_i, r, Lambda = 2^(d+5), k_v, r_FS exactly as in proof.md Section 1; exhaustive shift testing with n+6 tests per candidate for n <= 15) outputs the entire s with unconditional probability > 0.97 (in particular >= 2/3), and on every execution branch its total sequential work in the challenge model (classical bit operations, gate generation and addressing at ceil(log2(M+2)) per indexed access, exact Clifford+T gates with no synthesis, measurements, n+1 per source copy, all discarded copies and aborted runs) is T(N,s) = O(2^((17/6) sqrt(n)) n^5 log2 n). The uniform bit-length envelope B_T(n) = 2^((17/6) n^(1/2)) n^5 log2 n has growth index exactly 1/2. All logarithms base 2; n = ceil(log2 N); the outer big-O constant is absolute (independent of N, s and measurement outcomes); the exponent coefficient 17/6 is explicit and proved in proof.md Section 8. This holds jointly with the classical-space, quantum-space and sample bounds below for the same algorithm and parameters.

For the same algorithm the parity sieve PSieve of proof.md (Kuperberg-style low-bit pairing of labeled qubits with exact Hadamard-test Fourier labels, held-out parity and anchored odd-multiplier decoder; parameters d = ceil((3/4) sqrt n), l = ceil((n-3)/d), stage targets T^(j)_i, r, Lambda = 2^(d+5), k_v, r_FS exactly as in proof.md Section 1; exhaustive shift testing with n+6 tests per candidate for n <= 15), for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, the worst-case peak classical workspace (record arrays, merge-sort buffer, stored measurement records, counters, parameters; no stored circuit) is S_C(N,s) = O(2^((17/6) sqrt(n)) n^2 log2 n) bits. The envelope B_C(n) = 2^((17/6) n^(1/2)) n^2 log2 n has growth index exactly 1/2. All logarithms base 2; n = ceil(log2 N); the outer big-O constant is absolute (independent of N, s and measurement outcomes); the exponent coefficient 17/6 is explicit and proved in proof.md Section 8. This holds jointly with the stated time, quantum-space and sample bounds and success probability > 0.97.

For the same algorithm the parity sieve PSieve of proof.md (Kuperberg-style low-bit pairing of labeled qubits with exact Hadamard-test Fourier labels, held-out parity and anchored odd-multiplier decoder; parameters d = ceil((3/4) sqrt n), l = ceil((n-3)/d), stage targets T^(j)_i, r, Lambda = 2^(d+5), k_v, r_FS exactly as in proof.md Section 1; exhaustive shift testing with n+6 tests per candidate for n <= 15), for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, the worst-case peak number of allocated qubits (a pool of T_max labeled-qubit slots plus O(n) working qubits) is S_Q(N,s) = O(2^((17/6) sqrt(n)) n log2 n). The envelope B_Q(n) = 2^((17/6) n^(1/2)) n log2 n has growth index exactly 1/2. All logarithms base 2; n = ceil(log2 N); the outer big-O constant is absolute (independent of N, s and measurement outcomes); the exponent coefficient 17/6 is explicit and proved in proof.md Section 8. This holds jointly with the stated time, classical-space and sample bounds and success probability > 0.97.

For the same algorithm the parity sieve PSieve of proof.md (Kuperberg-style low-bit pairing of labeled qubits with exact Hadamard-test Fourier labels, held-out parity and anchored odd-multiplier decoder; parameters d = ceil((3/4) sqrt n), l = ceil((n-3)/d), stage targets T^(j)_i, r, Lambda = 2^(d+5), k_v, r_FS exactly as in proof.md Section 1; exhaustive shift testing with n+6 tests per candidate for n <= 15), for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, the total number Q(N,s) of fresh DCP source copies acquired on every execution branch, including rejected labels, discarded pairs, aborted runs and verification tests, is at most Q_max = sum_j 4 T^(j)_0 + Lambda k_v for n >= 16 (parameters as in proof.md Section 1) and at most N(n+6) <= 21*2^15 for n <= 15; hence Q(N,s) = O(2^((17/6) sqrt(n)) n^2 log2 n). The envelope B_samples(n) = 2^((17/6) n^(1/2)) n^2 log2 n has growth index exactly 1/2. All logarithms base 2; n = ceil(log2 N); the outer big-O constant is absolute (independent of N, s and measurement outcomes); the exponent coefficient 17/6 is explicit and proved in proof.md Section 8. This holds jointly with the stated total-work and workspace bounds and unconditional full-secret success probability > 0.97.

For the same algorithm (PSieve of proof.md), the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n)=0: all Q source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N and s, full-secret recovery succeeds with probability > 0.97 jointly with all four resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted; this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
